body.en: Conics in standard and general form, transformations, and polar coordinates are tested on advanced ACT and ACT subject items.
Convert the polar point \( \left(4,\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) \) to Cartesian. \[ x=4\cos\tfrac{\pi}{3}=4\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}=2,\quad y=4\sin\tfrac{\pi}{3}=4\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=2\sqrt3. \]

Completing the square converts a general conic to standard form. 3D distance: \(d = \sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2+(z_2-z_1)^2}\). A rotation of axes by \(\theta\) transforms \(x = X\cos\theta - Y\sin\theta\), \(y = X\sin\theta + Y\cos\theta\).

label.en: Worked example — Complete the square to find a circle

caption.en: The circle \( (x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 16 \) plotted on the Cartesian plane. The center is located at \( (h, k) = (3, -2) \) and the radius is \( r = \sqrt{16} = 4 \).

label.en: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — Coordinate Geometry & 3D Space

body.en:
• Center Signs & Radius in Circle Equations: In \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2\), the center is \((h, k)\). Watch the signs carefully: \((x - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 16\) has center \((3, -2)\), NOT \((-3, 2)\), and its radius is \(\sqrt{16} = 4\), NOT 16.
  • Perpendicular Slopes: Two lines are perpendicular if and only if their slopes are negative reciprocals: \(m_\perp = -1/m\). A common pitfall is forgetting the negative sign and taking merely the reciprocal.
  • Standard 2D Rotations About the Origin: A counterclockwise rotation of \(90°\) maps \((x, y) \to (-y, x)\); \(180°\) maps \((x, y) \to (-x, -y)\); and \(270°\) (or \(90°\) clockwise) maps \((x, y) \to (y, -x)\).
  • 3D Distance Extension: Do not collapse 3D distance into 2D: \(d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2 + (z_2 - z_1)^2}\). All three coordinate differences must be squared.

question.en: Find the distance between points \(A(1,2,3)\) and \(B(4,6,3)\).
Find the standard equation \(Ax + By = C\) of the line perpendicular to \(3x - 4y = 12\) that passes through the midpoint of the line segment joining \(P(-2, 7)\) and \(Q(6, 1)\).

solution.en:
(a) Midpoint \(M\): \[ M = \left( \dfrac{-2 + 6}{2}, \dfrac{7 + 1}{2} \right) = \left( \dfrac{4}{2}, \dfrac{8}{2} \right) = (2, 4). \]

(b) Perpendicular slope: Rewrite the given line in slope-intercept form: \(4y = 3x - 12 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{3}{4}x - 3\). The slope is \(m = \dfrac{3}{4}\). The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal: \(m_\perp = -\dfrac{4}{3}\).

(c) Line equation: Using point-slope form with point \((2, 4)\): \[ y - 4 = -\dfrac{4}{3}(x - 2) \implies 3(y - 4) = -4(x - 2) \implies 3y - 12 = -4x + 8 \implies 4x + 3y = 20. \]
